description:
COUSR02C case20 of 20 - THE `WHEN OTHER` ARM OF THE ORDERED `EVALUATE EIBAID` AT `app/cbl/COUSR02C.cbl:108-131`. An attention identifier the program never names arrives on a re-entry, so COUSR02C raises its error flag, moves the CSMSG01Y invalid-key literal into WS-MESSAGE and repaints the Update User screen exactly once. It reads no dataset, writes no dataset, issues no XCTL and leaves RETURN-CODE at 0. This is the twentieth and final case of parity/COUSR02C/, completing gate G15's twenty-per-program count.

PROVENANCE - STATICALLY DERIVED, NEVER EXECUTED (practice B12, risk R-A). Every value below was produced by structured reading of the COBOL and cross-checked against five authoritative sources: the paragraph text of `app/cbl/COUSR02C.cbl`; the byte layout of `app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23`; the `xxxI` PICTURE clauses of `app/cpy-bms/COUSR02.CPY`; the `DFHMDF` definitions of `app/bms/COUSR02.bms`; and the in-stream seed rows of `app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44`. Nothing here was captured from, recorded against or replayed from an execution of the legacy program, which AAP 0.7.6 shows is impossible in this environment across eight independently verified blockers - among them no z/OS or CICS runtime, a COBOL compiler whose indexed-file handler reports itself disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services, and the absence of the IBM-supplied DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR copybooks that COUSR02C copies at :67-68. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the case count, the field-for-field diff and the diff-count-equals-zero gate are untouched.

UNIT UNDER TEST. `user.UserUpdateController`, invoked as a plain Java object through its handler method with a fixture-backed `user.SecUserRepository` constructor-injected - `unitKind` is `CONTROLLER_POJO`, so there is no MockMvc, no servlet container, no web application context and no JobLauncher anywhere in the path (gate G51). COUSR02C keeps its decision logic in the program itself rather than in a separate service, which is why the controller and not a service is the unit here.

PATH PINNED, STATEMENT BY STATEMENT. EIBCALEN is 194 and therefore non-zero, so MAIN-PARA takes the ELSE at :93 and `MOVE DFHCOMMAREA(1:EIBCALEN) TO CARDDEMO-COMMAREA` at :94 copies the whole commarea in. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1, so CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is true, the `IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER` at :95 is false and control takes the ELSE at :106 to `PERFORM RECEIVE-USRUPD-SCREEN` at :107. RECEIVE-USRUPD-SCREEN (:283-291) captures RESP(WS-RESP-CD) and RESP2(WS-REAS-CD), AND NOTHING AFTERWARDS EVER TESTS EITHER OF THEM; that untested response code is inherited behaviour and is preserved verbatim rather than tidied into a check the COBOL does not perform (practice B5). Control then reaches `EVALUATE EIBAID` at :108.

GATE G30 - `WHEN OTHER` IS LAST, AND IS REACHED ONLY BY DECLINING FIVE ARMS IN SOURCE ORDER. The EVALUATE names exactly five attention identifiers, in this order: DFHENTER (:109, PROCESS-ENTER-KEY), DFHPF3 (:111, UPDATE-USER-INFO then RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN), DFHPF4 (:120, CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN), DFHPF5 (:122, UPDATE-USER-INFO) and DFHPF12 (:124, RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN via COADM01C); `WHEN OTHER` at :127-130 is the sixth and LAST arm. The AID presented here is DFHPF9, EBCDIC 0xF9 per `common.CicsAid`, and DFHPF9 occurs zero times anywhere in `app/cbl` - its only occurrence in this repository is a branch of `app/cpy/CSSTRPFY.cpy`, which COUSR02C does not copy. So the first five arms are each evaluated and each declines, and only then does `WHEN OTHER` fire. That the key is unadvertised is corroborated by the screen's own footer, `app/bms/COUSR02.bms:163-164`, which offers only 'ENTER=Fetch  F3=Save&&Exit  F4=Clear  F5=Save  F12=Cancel'. Taken with case04 (DFHENTER), cases 17-18 (DFHPF3), case14 (DFHPF4), cases 07-13 and 15-16 (DFHPF5) and case19 (DFHPF12), ALL SIX ARMS OF THE ORDERED EVALUATE ARE NOW COVERED, and this case is the folder's proof that the default arm sits last and is not reachable by fall-through.

THE ARM'S THREE STATEMENTS, AND NOTHING ELSE. :128 `MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG` sets ERR-FLG-ON. :129 `MOVE CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY TO WS-MESSAGE` takes the CSMSG01Y literal. :130 `PERFORM SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN` repaints the map ONCE. SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN (:266-278) performs POPULATE-HEADER-INFO, moves WS-MESSAGE to ERRMSGO and issues a single `EXEC CICS SEND MAP('COUSR2A') MAPSET('COUSR02') FROM(COUSR2AO) ERASE CURSOR`. Control then falls out of END-EVALUATE and both END-IFs to :135-138 `EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CU02') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)`.

MESSAGE WIDTH CHAIN, THE TEXT IS FORTY CHARACTERS. `app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy:20-21` declares `CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY PIC X(50)` with the literal 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...' followed by nine spaces inside the quotes, so the source literal is 49 characters and COBOL supplies one more space to fill the field: 40 + 9 + 1 = 50. THE TEXT IS FORTY CHARACTERS, NOT THIRTY-NINE - counted mechanically including the three-dot ellipsis, and corroborated independently by `common.SystemMessages.CCDA_MSG_INVALID_KEY`, which composes the same 40 + 9 + 1 and warns a reader to recount before assuming thirty-nine. The chain is then `CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY PIC X(50)` -> `WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80)` (a further 30 spaces of left-justified pad) -> `ERRMSGO PIC X(78)` at :270, an X(80)-to-X(78) RIGHT TRUNCATION that discards two trailing spaces and no text. The single `expectedMessages` entry is therefore the complete 78-byte ERRMSG image: 40 characters of text followed by 38 spaces, byte-exact and untrimmed, exactly as the contract requires. This is the only case in parity/COUSR02C/ that consumes `common.SystemMessages`; every other message on this screen is an inline literal in COUSR02C itself.

THE SENT PAYLOAD - THE TWELVE `xxxI` ITEMS AND THEIR EXPECTED VALUES. `app/cpy-bms/COUSR02.CPY:91` declares `01 COUSR2AO REDEFINES COUSR2AI`, and each field occupies the same span on both views (input 2 + 1 + 4 + n against output 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + n, both 7 + n), so every `xxxO` item IS the bytes of its `xxxI` item. The echo below is therefore a consequence of REDEFINES rather than an assumption. POPULATE-HEADER-INFO (:296-315) writes the six header items and the arm writes ERRMSG; the five detail items are neither blanked nor repopulated on this path, so they return exactly as received. Expected values, at their declared widths: TRNNAME X(4) = 'CU02' (WS-TRANID, :302); TITLE01 X(40) = '      AWS Mainframe Modernization       ' (CCDA-TITLE01, :300); CURDATE X(8) = '07/19/22' (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY, :309); PGMNAME X(8) = 'COUSR02C' (WS-PGMNAME, :303); TITLE02 X(40) = '              CardDemo                  ' (CCDA-TITLE02, :301); CURTIME X(8) = '23:12:34' (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS, :315); USRIDIN X(8) = 'USER0001'; FNAME X(20) = 'LAWRENCE' padded to 20; LNAME X(20) = 'THOMAS' padded to 20; PASSWD X(8) = 'PASSWORD'; USRTYPE X(1) = 'U'; ERRMSG X(78) = the 78-byte invalid-key image above. The payload is those twelve items and no others: `xxxL`, `xxxF` and `xxxA` are length, flag and attribute METADATA used for validation and highlighting and are never payload members, and the item is spelled USRIDIN throughout - never USERID.

NO HIGHLIGHT, NO COLOUR MOVE, NO CURSOR (gate G38). COUSR02C does not copy CSSETATY - its COPY list at :49-68 is COCOM01Y, COUSR02, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CSUSR01Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - so no shared highlight routine exists to apply. Its three colour moves onto ERRMSGC are inline and every one is on a different path: DFHRED at :241 inside UPDATE-USER-INFO's nothing-was-modified branch, DFHNEUTR at :338 on a successful READ-USER-SEC-FILE, DFHGREEN at :371 on a successful UPDATE-USER-SEC-FILE. The `WHEN OTHER` arm at :127-130 touches ERRMSGC not at all, so NO `MOVE DFHRED` is asserted here. The field still renders red, but from the map default at `app/bms/COUSR02.bms:155-158`, `ERRMSG DFHMDF ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET) COLOR=RED LENGTH=78 POS=(23,1)` - a property of the mapset, not an act of the program. Equally there is NO cursor position set: every `MOVE -1 TO xxxL` in this program lives in PROCESS-ENTER-KEY (:150, :153), in UPDATE-USER-INFO (:184, :190, :196, :202, :208, :211) or in the first-entry branch (:98), and all of those are bypassed. This case is a REENTER invocation whose error path applies no highlight at all, and asserting one would invent behaviour the COBOL does not have (practice B5).

REQUEST STATE AND STATELESSNESS (gate G37, rule R6). The commarea, the AID and the screen values all travel in the payload; no server-side session state exists. `jobParameters` carries the complete 194-byte commarea field by field, and the declared widths sum to exactly 194 - COCOM01Y's 34 + 84 + 12 + 16 + 14 = 160 plus the 34-byte CDEMO-CU02-INFO extension declared at `COUSR02C.cbl:50-58` - which is where EIBCALEN = 194 comes from. That 34-byte extension rides on the DTO, not on the shared 160-byte `common.NavigationContext`. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT stays 1 on the response, because the arm never resets it and only RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN (:257) moves ZEROS there, so the next interaction re-enters the REENTER branch. NO `nextProgram` IS PRODUCED: control reaches `EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CU02')` at :135, not an XCTL, and CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM is left exactly as it arrived, so the operator stays on this screen.

WHERE THE REQUEST CAME FROM, DERIVED NOT INVENTED. `app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl:66-75` declares CDEMO-CU00-INFO with a layout byte-identical to CDEMO-CU02-INFO - X(08), X(08), 9(08), X(01), X(01), X(08) - so the same 34 bytes are read under either name. At `COUSR00C.cbl:178-197` a selection flag of 'U' moves 'COUSR02C' to CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, WS-TRANID 'CU00' to CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, WS-PGMNAME 'COUSR00C' to CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM and 0 to CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT, then XCTLs. COUSR02C's first pass therefore took the not-REENTER branch at :95-105: it set REENTER, moved LOW-VALUES to COUSR2AO, moved -1 to USRIDINL, found CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED non-blank at :99, moved it to USRIDINI and performed PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, which read USER0001 from USRSEC and painted FNAME, LNAME, PASSWD and USRTYPE from that record (:167-170). THIS case is the pass that follows. All five detail fields carry FSET in the mapset - USRIDIN :85, FNAME :103, LNAME :116, PASSWD :130 as DRK,FSET,UNPROT, USRTYPE :145 - so the terminal retransmits them unchanged, and the operator pressed an unadvertised key. The list-window fields CDEMO-CU02-USRID-FIRST, -USRID-LAST, -PAGE-NUM and -NEXT-PAGE-FLG carry the one full page COUSR00C had displayed - ten seeded users at a page size of ten - and COUSR02C references none of the four anywhere; they travel because the extension travels intact. CDEMO-CUSTOMER-INFO, CDEMO-ACCOUNT-INFO, CDEMO-CARD-INFO and CDEMO-MORE-INFO are likewise untouched by this program and are carried at the neutral value for their PICTURE - zeros for a PIC 9 span, spaces for a PIC X span - since no program on this path writes them. CDEMO-LAST-MAP and CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET are deliberately spaces rather than 'COUSR2A' and 'COUSR02': those two fields are referenced only by COACTUPC, COACTVWC, COCRDLIC, COCRDSLC and COCRDUPC, and grep gives zero occurrences in each of COSGN00C, COADM01C, COMEN01C, COUSR00C and COUSR02C, so naming the map there would assert a write that no program on this path performs (practice B5).

NO DATASET ACCESS AT ALL (gates G44, G47). `UPDATE-USER-INFO` (:177), `READ-USER-SEC-FILE` (:320) and `UPDATE-USER-SEC-FILE` (:358) are the only paragraphs that touch USRSEC, and the `WHEN OTHER` arm performs none of them. This case's contribution to G47 is therefore the NO-CALL state of both call sites: `readForUpdate` is invoked ZERO times and `rewrite` is invoked ZERO times. `expectedRecords` consequently pins all ten seeded rows at their seed values, which asserts something stronger than absence of a write - the dataset was never even read. No record is added, no record is deleted, no field changes, and no version column, DDL or migration exists to change (gate G44). Nor is there any re-read-and-compare: COUSR02C has NO `9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC` paragraph - grep confirms zero occurrences - so gate G43's optimistic-concurrency check scopes to the account and card packages only and is correctly absent here.

RECORD GEOMETRY (gates G19, G21). Each of the ten expectations carries the full 80-byte SEC-USER-DATA field set in copybook declaration order, plus the complete 80-byte record image so the TOTAL WIDTH is asserted and not merely the field values. The offsets are summed mechanically from `app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23` (practice B11): SEC-USR-ID X(08) at 1-8, SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) at 9-28, SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) at 29-48, SEC-USR-PWD X(08) at 49-56, SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) at 57, SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) at 58-80, giving 57 + 23 = 80 - corroborated by `app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:64-66` `KEYS(8,0) RECORDSIZE(80,80)` and by :48 `DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB)`. SEC-USR-FILLER IS A NAMED FIELD, NOT AN ANONYMOUS FILLER, so it appears BY NAME in every one of the ten field maps holding exactly 23 spaces; the 80-byte total is the self-check that it was emitted, since a record missing that span would be short by exactly 23 (gate G21). All six fields are PIC X, so there is no COMP-3, no scale, no rounding mode and no zoned sign overpunch anywhere in this case - AAP rules R2, R3 and R4 have no subject here.

SEED DATA AND NORMALISATION. `inputs` declares the ten USRSEC records INLINE rather than naming a fixture, because USRSEC is the one dataset in the application with no ASCII fixture file; the rows are reproduced verbatim from `app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44` and each measures exactly 57 bytes. `normalisations` therefore declares USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80, which supplies the absent SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) as spaces before any comparison. Row indices are zero-based, ADMIN001 at 0 through USER0005 at 9. Every password is the literal eight-character 'PASSWORD' and is carried in PLAINTEXT, exactly as `SEC-USR-PWD PIC X(08)` holds it and exactly as COSGN00C compares it: hashing it would be a behaviour change and Spring Security is out of scope (gate G41, practice B6). These are 2022-vintage demo values from a public sample repository, they guard nothing, and they never leave the test JVM. The dataset is addressed only by its logical binding key USRSEC, and no fully-qualified mainframe DSNAME literal appears anywhere in this fixture (gate G46). Text is US-ASCII throughout - the encoding is stated rather than inherited from a platform default (practice B8).

RETURN CODE. `expectedReturnCode` is 0. COUSR02C contains zero `CALL 'CEE3ABD'` sites, so gate G35 does not apply to it; an unrecognised keystroke is a screen-level error reported through ERRMSG, not an abend. The program also contains zero `GO TO` statements, so gate G32's restructuring requirement does not apply, and it paginates nothing, so gate G39 does not apply.

RULES. `review_rules` returns the single line 'No user rules provided', so no project-specific rule governs this fixture. Its absence is stated rather than passed over in silence and is not treated as licence to lower the bar: the work is held instead to the enterprise practices AAP 0.10.2 substitutes - B1 no placeholders, B3 the reference trees read-only and unmodified, B4 no silent normalisation (which is why the forty-character count is corrected out loud rather than quietly followed), B5 inherited behaviour preserved including the untested RECEIVE response code, B6 the plaintext password left as the legacy design has it, B7 the clock pinned so the run is reproducible, B8 explicit field-to-value pairs and an explicit encoding, B11 every offset summed mechanically, and B12 honest static-derivation provenance.

NOTE TO A REVIEWER GREPPING THIS FIXTURE. Nine tokens appear in this description ONLY as prohibition notices, never as data, and every occurrence is a negative statement: DFHENTER, DFHPF3, DFHPF4, DFHPF5 and DFHPF12 are named to record that each was evaluated and DECLINED in source order before `WHEN OTHER` fired; DFHRED is named to record that NO colour move happens on this path; nextProgram is named to record that NONE is produced; MockMvc is named to record that it is NOT used; and USERID is named to record that the payload item is spelled USRIDIN and never USERID. They are stated out loud rather than left implicit so the next engineer learns they are excluded rather than merely unused. The machine-checkable invariant is the complement: outside `description`, the only AID token in this fixture is DFHPF9, the only payload identifier is USRIDIN, and none of the ten distinct inline error literals COUSR02C carries across twelve sites - :148, :182, :188, :194, :200, :206, :239, :336, :342, :349, :379 and :386 - appears anywhere in it.
expectedMessages: Invalid key pressed. Please see below...
